title: Silent validation of encoded pairs
statement: Let $M$ be a Boolean finite Turing machine, let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$, and let $r$ be a Boolean word. For every split $x=u r$, there exist an integer time $t\le |r|+1$ such that the controller started in its silent validation state at input position $|u|+1$ has the following behavior: if the pair parser succeeds on $r$, then for some input-head position $p$ its configuration after $t$ steps is the corresponding configuration with the same simulated tape contents, empty output, input head at $p$, and controller state for the next phase. If the parser fails on $r$, then after $t$ steps the controller is halted and its output is empty.
replaced:
For a split $x = p s$ of the input, there is a time $t \le \abs{s} + 1$ from
the controller's silent validation state at position $\abs{p}$ such that: if
$s$ is a valid word of the self-delimiting pair code, after $t$ steps the
controller is at its post-validation state with nothing emitted; and if $s$
is malformed, after $t$ steps the controller has halted with empty output.
